title: pasta: outbound IPv6 refused (RST) with static --address networking; v4-only -a silently disables guest IPv6
body:
On Fedora 44 with podman 5.8.4 and pasta 0^20260728.gf8df3f1 (rootless, single-NIC host) I hit two related behaviors around static pasta addressing. I could not find an existing ticket for either; passt bug 47 and podman issues 27125 and 14709 are the closest I found.

### What I run

My pods use explicit v4 addressing because with default pasta the host's only IPv4 is copied into the namespace, which makes the host unreachable from containers:

```
--network pasta:-a,10.0.2.100,-g,10.0.2.1
```

### Symptom 1: v4-only static addressing silently disables guest IPv6

With that config the guest has no IPv6 at all, but DNS still returns AAAA records for public names. Anything that resolves v6-first and does not fall back (for example node 18 based images, whose http client tries only the first resolved address) fails with ECONNREFUSED against every IPv6 destination, including the host's own addresses. This took down an uptime-kuma monitor that connects to the host by name.

### Symptom 2: with dual-stack static addressing, outbound public IPv6 is refused while everything else works

pasta's -a and -g can be given once per family, so I tried dual-stack static addressing:

```
--network pasta:-a,10.0.3.5,-g,10.0.3.1,-a,fd00:10:0:2::5,-g,fd00:10:0:2::1
```

The guest then gets both addresses plus a default v6 route:

```
default via fd00:10:0:2::1 dev enp1s0 metric 1024
```

From inside such a container (node fetch, one run):

```
https://[2606:4700:4700::1111]/   -> ECONNREFUSED
http://[2606:4700:4700::1111]/    -> ECONNREFUSED
host's own ULA address, port 8095 -> 200
host's IPv4 address, port 8095    -> 200
outbound IPv4 (http://1.1.1.1/)   -> works
```

So with static addressing, host-local IPv6 works and outbound IPv4 works, but outbound public IPv6 gets an RST rather than a timeout or an ICMPv6 unreachable. In the v4-only case there is no signal at all that IPv6 is gone.

### What I expected

Either outbound IPv6 works with static addressing the same way outbound IPv4 does, or the failure is visible (ICMPv6 unreachable instead of RST) and documented. The pasta man page describes -a as "can be specified zero to two times (for IPv4 and IPv6)" but does not say that passing only an IPv4 address removes guest IPv6 entirely, which is a trap for exactly the users who reach for static addressing.

### Workaround

I pinned the one hostname I need to the host's IPv4 in the pod's /etc/hosts and kept the v4-only addressing.

Happy to test patches or gather more data (tcpdump on the host side, pasta debug logs).
